Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list and congrats on choosing Redwood.

Quick summary of what I'm attaching and the proposed next steps:

1) DPA: attached is our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_Skyridge_20261118.pdf). We can accept e-sign via DocuSign; I've created a signing envelope below. If your legal needs to redline, loop in Lauren and we'll coordinate. Note: our standard DPA includes data processing and subprocessors clauses; we usually agree minor redlines under procurement review.

2) SOC 2: here is a secure read-only link to our latest SOC 2 report — SOC2 reports are view-only to invited reviewers (redwood link below). If you need a bound copy, we can provide an auditor contact.

3) Subprocessors: attached CSV lists current subprocessors and their roles. Data residency: primary customer data is in us-west (AWS) with backups replicated in us-central only; we do not use third-country transfers beyond those regions for Skyridge by default. If you have strict residency requirements, let us know and we can propose options.

4) PO & invoicing: Redwood accepts your standard PO. Billing contact: invoices@redwood.com. Remit address: Redwood Inference, 432 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94104. Standard term: Net 30; for Net 45 please indicate on PO. Ben is cc'd for billing/finance approvals.

Next steps I suggest:
- We send DocuSign DPA to your legal (link below) — if OK, sign and return
- Skyridge creates PO and provides PO number to invoices@redwood.com
- We'll provision account access once PO number and signed DPA are received

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Skyridge_20261118.pdf, subprocessor_declaration.csv
Links: https://redwood-security-reports.example.com/soc2/2026, DocuSign envelope: https://na1.docusign.net/Signing/Document/abc123

Best,

Thanks Marcus — quick clarification from our security team:

- We need to confirm whether 'TelemetryOps' (listed as a subprocessor) has access to any PHI. If so we will need an additional BAA or explicit confirmation that TelemetryOps does not touch PHI.
- Also confirm backup retention windows and whether backups are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys.

Can Lauren or Ben confirm those two points? We're trying to keep legal/IT review light if answers are clear.

Appreciate it,

Elaine

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Harper <elaine.harper@skyridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial security pack & PO info request for Redwood

Hi Elaine — looping in with the two confirmations:

- TelemetryOps: does not process or store PHI. Their access is limited to anonymized metrics pipelines (latency/uptime) and they never receive customer payloads. We can provide a subprocessors attestation with their SOC report on request.

- Backups & keys: Backups are encrypted at rest using AES-256. For Skyridge we can enable customer-managed keys (CMK) via your KMS — please indicate if you'd like CMK enabled and Ben will coordinate the technical handoff. Retention default is 30 days for rolling backups and 90 days for cold snapshots, but retention can be adjusted per contract.

If that covers security, I'll proceed to send the DocuSign envelope to your legal contact and Ben will confirm billing routing for the PO once you provide the PO number.

Regards,

Lauren Bishop
Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: subprocessors_attestation.pdf (pdf)]
